Their starship, the Veskan Scourge, loomed menacingly on our flank as they opened fire with their weapon batteries. My heart raced as I ducked for cover behind the helm station console.

Our quick response saved us from being crippled or worse. The engineering team managed to divert power from non-essential systems to the defenses. With a resolve point investment, I activated our class 3 energy shields, absorbing most of the incoming damage. The Vesk ship seemed determined to teach us a lesson, but they underestimated our resolve and our ability to adapt. After a grueling Starship Combat encounter, we emerged victorious. However, our victory came at a steep price; several crew members were injured, and the Vesk managed to escape before we could board their ship.

Once back onboard the DS2 Nightingale, we tended to the wounded, taking care to restore their stamina through medical attention and food. Rest was a precious commodity, but it was essential to ensure that our crew remained operational. We continued our approach to the derelict vessel, our determination undeterred. This encounter served as a grim reminder of the risks we take every day in service to the Starfinder Society, but it also reaffirmed our commitment to our mission. We will not be deterred, and we will continue to seek out knowledge and adventure in the vast expanse of the galaxy.

With the immediate threat quelled, we took stock of our situation. The memorial site had been secured, but the reason for the Aeon Guard's presence remains a mystery. We shall investigate further, but until then, the Neptune's Grace continues its journey in pursuit of knowledge and adventure.

Upon re-entry into normal space, I assessed the situation and reported the incident to Starfinder Society Command, requesting additional assistance to secure the Castrovel system and investigate the energy signature. input: Azlanti stealth fleet detected near Triaxus. Pact Worlds on high alert. orders incoming from Absalom Station.
output:
Personal Log Stardate 9815.63

The azure skies of Triaxus' orbital station blurred by as I settled in for another long day at my console aboard the Starfinder Society ship, the _Mistborn_. My fingers danced over the keys, recording society data and scanning for anomalous activity within the sector. Suddenly, an unusual blip appeared on the radar. A fleet of ships, cloaked and moving silently through the vacuum. The azure hulls gleamed faintly with a familiar iridescence - the markings of the Azlanti Star Empire.

My heart raced, and I quickly reported the sighting to our captain. We were far from the nearest Pact Worlds outpost; we would have to act fast if we wanted to avoid being caught in their crossfire. With a flick of switches, I initiated emergency jump drive, and the _Mistborn_ lurched forward as we entered the chaotic maelstrom of drift travel.

As the _Mistborn_ jumped away from the approaching fleet, I quickly relayed the situation to Absalom Station, requesting further instructions while monitoring our own defenses. The ancient technology of the Azlanti was known for its lethality, especially when it came to starship combat. Our ship, though well-maintained, would not last long against their relentless assault.

With each passing moment, the tension grew thicker in the air. The captain called for all hands to battle stations, and we prepared for the worst. As I braced myself, I took a deep breath, focusing my resolve points and steadying my nerves, knowing that our only chance lay in our ability to outmaneuver these elusive adversaries.

Just then, clear orders arrived from the Society: evade and report back to Absalom Station. Gathering our collective strength, we pushed the _Mistborn_ to its limits, zigzagging through the galaxy to avoid detection. Though we were fast, the Azlantis pursued us relentlessly, their stealth technology allowing them to remain one step ahead. But, with the Society's resources at our disposal, we were determined to make it home, no matter what.

The chase continued, our stamina dwindling, but our resolve never faltered. We knew that if we could reach Absalom Station, we would have a fighting chance. In the end, our determination paid off; we made it back to Pact Worlds space, safe and sound. And as I sit here now, recording this log, I am reminded once again of the true power of the Starfinder Society - unity, resourcefulness, and the unyielding spirit of adventure.

End Log.

Thankfully, due to our recent hull upgrades, the breach did not expand, and we only experienced a minor loss of atmosphere. I immediately called for repairs, allocating 10 resolve points from the ship's reserve to expedite the process. Our skilled mechanic, Jax, quickly got to work, using his stellar mechanics skill to patch up the hull with minimal fuss. Now, as we approach Triaxus trading post, I cannot help but reflect on the importance of our hull maintenance and the value of investing in quality starship components. While the micro-meteorite impact caused only a minor setback, it serves as a stark reminder of the potential dangers lurking in the unforgiving expanse of space. As we prepare to dock at Triaxus and resume our duties as Society field recorders, I am grateful for the resilience and resourcefulness of our crew and the superiority of our vessel, which enabled us to weather this unexpected storm.

As we sailed through the vast expanse of space, the eerie silence was disturbed by the unexpected appearance of a spectral vessel on our sensors. Log Entry 17-B, Lorekeeper Kaela Daz

The stars of the Perilous Sands Nebula glittered around us like diamonds on black velvet as we approached the waystation. The last leg of our journey had been uneventful, save for the brief encounter with the gnome stowaway who'd attempted to pilfer our cargo. I resolved the issue swiftly and we continued on our course. However, my peaceful contemplation was soon disrupted by an unexpected finding.

Upon entering the Drift Beacon's range, I detected an anomaly in its encrypted data streams. Using my enhanced decryption abilities, I managed to crack the encryption within minutes. To my shock, the beacon broadcasted a distress signal, not a standard triangulation sequence. Its origin was pinpointed to an uncharted derelict starship drifting nearby. Intrigued and compelled by duty to assist fellow explorers, I reported the discovery to Captain Valthrun and the rest of the crew.

Captain Valthrun ordered the helmsman to alter course towards the distressed vessel while I prepared our team for potential danger. I advised the crew to ready their plasma rifles and armor, just in case. With our preparations complete, we approached the derelict starship cautiously. Upon arrival, we were greeted by a desolate scene - the ship appeared abandoned, its hull peppered with small meteor impacts. But something didn't feel right; there was a palpable sense of unease that permeated the air.

As we boarded the ship, we discovered a scene of chaos and destruction. The crew quarters were ransacked, personal belongings scattered across the floor. It seemed as though they had been attacked without warning. A quick survey of the ship revealed no survivors, only remnants of what once was a thriving starship community. As we explored further, we stumbled upon a hidden laboratory filled with experimental technology. It was clear that this crew had been conducting groundbreaking research before their untimely demise.

With our investigation concluded, we returned to our own starship. My mind was heavy with thoughts of the unfortunate fate that befell these brave souls. Though it pained me to leave behind such important discoveries, I knew that I must report our findings back to the Starfinder Society. This tragedy served as another reminder of the perils that come with exploration, but also the importance of documenting history, even in its darkest corners.
